prompt: A cutoff sweep crosses several octaves using a linear ramp in hertz. The low octaves rush by while high octaves take most of the time. Which change gives equal time to each octave?

options.text: Ramp in octave units, then convert to frequency
options.explanation: Correct. Equal octave steps mean equal frequency ratios, matching the requested timing.

options.text: Use a longer linear-in-hertz ramp without changing the mapping
options.explanation: That slows the whole sweep but keeps the same unequal share per octave.

options.text: Update the linear-in-hertz ramp less often
options.explanation: That adds coarser steps without correcting the musical-unit mapping.
Signal level does not change the cutoff trajectory’s frequency spacing.

workedExample: Each successive octave spans twice as many hertz as the preceding one. A constant hertz-per-second rate therefore spends progressively longer on upper octaves. Interpolate in octaves when equal intervals should receive equal time; use an explicit endpoint policy if a gain fade must reach zero.
